content.stem: The CSWIP scheme is administered by:
distractors: BINDT administers PCN.
NRCan administers the Canadian scheme.
ASNT operates the American schemes.
content.explanation: CSWIP, Certification Scheme for Weldment Inspection Personnel, is administered by TWI Certification Ltd.

content.stem: CSWIP NDT certification is based on the same technical standard as PCN, namely:
distractors: SNT-TC-1A is the ASNT employer based practice.
CAN/CGSB-48.9712 is the Canadian adoption of ISO 9712.
EN 4179 is the aerospace personnel standard.
content.explanation: Both are UK based central certification schemes operating to ISO 9712, which is why their level structures and validity periods match.

content.stem: CSWIP is best known outside NDT for its certification of:
options: Welding inspectors, under the 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2 designations
distractors: Radiation protection supervision is a separate regulatory role.
CSWIP does certify painting inspectors, but that is not the best known scope.
Procedures are qualified under the ISO 15614 series, not certified by CSWIP.
content.explanation: CSWIP 3.1 Welding Inspector and CSWIP 3.2 Senior Welding Inspector are the scheme's most widely held qualifications.

content.stem: A CSWIP Welding Inspector qualification differs from a CSWIP NDT method certificate in that it:
options: Covers visual inspection and the supervision of weld quality rather than a specific NDT method
distractors: It is issued at several grades, 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2.
Examination is required.
It is subject to renewal like other CSWIP certification.
content.explanation: The welding inspector qualification covers visual examination, codes and weld quality control; NDT method certificates cover the individual methods.

content.stem: Under both CSWIP and PCN, a certificate issued to ISO 9712 is valid for:
distractors: Three years is not the ISO 9712 period.
One year is the vision test interval.
Ten years is the recertification interval, which is two periods.
content.explanation: The five year validity is set by ISO 9712 and applies to both schemes, with recertification at ten years.

content.stem: A candidate holding PCN Level 2 in ultrasonics who wishes to hold CSWIP Level 2 in the same method:
options: Must apply to CSWIP and satisfy its requirements; the certificates are not interchangeable
distractors: Automatic transfer between certification bodies does not exist.
Prerequisites apply to each application.
Holding certificates from more than one body is permitted.
content.explanation: The schemes are separate certification bodies. Common technical roots aid recognition but do not create automatic transfer.

content.stem: Under both ISO 9712 based schemes, the employer's written authorisation is:
options: Still required before the certified person operates on the employer's products
distractors: The certificate does not discharge the employer's authorisation duty.
Authorisation is a requirement, not an option.
The certification body does not issue employer authorisations.
content.explanation: Certification evidences generic competence; the employer authorises work on its own equipment, procedures and products.

content.stem: The principal advantage of an ISO 9712 based scheme such as PCN, CSWIP or CGSB over an employer based scheme is:
options: Independence of the certifying body and portability of the certificate
distractors: Central schemes are generally more expensive to obtain.
Minimum training durations are set by the standard.
Examination is central to the model.
content.explanation: Independence and portability are the defining features, and they are why these certificates are specified on international projects.
